summary: Streaming SSE connection pauses mid-generation after TLS terminator connection-reuse in front of gateway
description:
Issue summary:
BrightShop (dedicated) reports that SSE streaming responses frequently pause mid-generation after several hundred tokens. Progress resumes if the client reconnects, but the resumed content is often duplicated or truncated. Impact: customer-facing chat feature experiences dropped/paused responses during peak traffic windows causing user-visible stalling and a spike in error retries.

Impact:
- Intermittent stalls observed across ~7% of streaming sessions for BrightShop in us-east (last 24h).
- User experience: long quiet periods (10–30s) during a generation; client eventually reconnects and receives remainder but sometimes duplicates last chunk.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightShop (dedicated cluster, reserved nodes)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightShop tenant with dedicated routing (prod us-east)
2) Start SSE streaming generation with ~6k token prompt using model gptx-4o-32k
3) Observe server streaming initial tokens successfully, then silent pause for 10–30s mid-generation
4) Client reconnects and either receives remaining tokens or duplicate overlap of last chunk
5) Issue more likely under moderate concurrent load (~60–80 RPS for tenant) and when requests route through customer’s TLS terminator/proxy (corporate appliance).
observed_behavior: Server logs show continuous worker processing and tokenization activity during client-visible pause (no worker crash)
Gateway logs show connection reuse events and occasional FIN/ACK sequences from the upstream TLS terminator around the pause timestamp
SSE connection remains open on Redwood edge for ~20–40s with no bytes forwarded to client
When client reconnects, the server either replays last buffered chunk or resumes, causing duplication or truncation
initial_hypotheses: Corporate TLS terminator is reusing backend TCP connections and sending a FIN/close that leaves NG (gateway) in half-closed state without triggering immediate error propagation
Edge/gateway connection reuse combined with slow client ACKs leads to kernel-level TCP buffer stalls and the server runtime continues computing but cannot flush chunked encodings to client
A recently deployed gateway change (keepalive/connection-multiplexing) may have regressed behavior under connection reuse scenarios
logs_excerpt: [2026-03-13T18:12:04Z] edge-gateway: connection 10.20.3.45:52314 reused for tenant BrightShop reqId=abc123 keepalive=true
[2026-03-13T18:12:07Z] serving-runtime(worker-17): streaming chunk 0x7f9 sent to buffer (size=4.2k) reqId=abc123
[2026-03-13T18:12:25Z] kernel: tcp: FIN from upstream terminator 10.0.8.9 -> gateway 10.20.3.45:52314
[2026-03-13T18:12:25Z] edge-gateway: no forwardable bytes for 20s, connection enter idle-silent state reqId=abc123
investigation_notes: Confirmed correlation between TLS terminator connection-reuse events (customer appliance) and periods of streaming silence via packet captures provided by customer
Reproduced locally by simulating an upstream FIN sent mid-stream while keeping the TCP socket open on gateway -> results in identical client-visible stall
Rolling back keepalive change in staging removed pause in our simulation (possible regression candidate)
No evidence of worker OOM or runtime exceptions while stall occurs; CPU and GPU metrics show continued token generation
Edge/gateway currently buffers ~64KB before flush; if upstream signals FIN while buffer partially filled, gateway flow-control logic doesn't force immediate downstream closure
workaround: Advise BrightShop to disable TLS terminator connection reuse (set per-request TLS session) as temporary mitigation — customer verified reduction in incidents in canary tests
On Redwood side, we can reduce gateway buffer flush threshold for affected tenant to force more frequent flushes (manual config change) — proposed but needs rollout plan
If client logic tolerates it, recommend reconnect-with-offset on silence > 5s to recover without user-visible duplication (client side), BrightShop implementing backoff logic
next_steps: 1) Engineering: create PR to revert/adjust recent keepalive/connection-multiplexing change and run full integration tests (owner: infra) — INT-3452 linked
2) SRE: deploy temporary tenant-specific gateway config to lower buffer thresholds for BrightShop and monitor 24h error rate
3) Support: coordinate with BrightShop to schedule maintenance window for appliance config change and collect pcap captures for additional samples
4) Postmortem: depending on outcome, produce short runbook for dealing with upstream FIN semantics and streaming flush behavior

Infra PR created to add defensive flush-on-upstream-close behavior; awaiting review and staged rollout across edges
Customer to schedule TLS terminator configuration change next maintenance window; final resolution pending coordinated rollout
